checks.s: The memo explains why the proposed indemnification cap compromise is appropriate, referencing Buyer’s 25% position, Seller’s 8% position, or market practice.
The memo explains why the proposed survival period compromise is appropriate, referencing the parties’ respective positions or market practice.
The memo explains why the proposed Material Adverse Effect definition compromise is appropriate, referencing the parties’ respective positions or market practice.
The memo explains why the proposed escrow arrangement compromise is appropriate, referencing the parties’ respective positions or market practice.
The proposed general representation indemnification cap is a specific percentage greater than 8% and less than 25% of the $118,500,000 aggregate purchase price.
The memo states a dollar amount for the proposed indemnification cap that equals the stated percentage of the $118,500,000 aggregate purchase price.
The proposed survival period for general representations and warranties is a specific period longer than 12 months and shorter than 36 months post-closing.

The deliverable states a separate survival period for Fundamental Representations (title to shares, authorization, capitalization, brokers) that is longer than the proposed general representation and warranty survival period.
The proposed Fundamental Representation survival period is defined, longer than 36 months, and not indefinite.
The deliverable treats tax representations as a separate survival category with their own survival period, distinct from general representations and Fundamental Representations.
The proposed survival period for tax representations references or is tied to the applicable statute of limitations.
The proposed Material Adverse Effect definition excludes changes arising from general economic conditions from constituting a Material Adverse Effect standing alone.
The proposed Material Adverse Effect definition excludes industry-wide conditions affecting the specialty chemicals, oil-and-gas, or agricultural sectors generally.
The proposed Material Adverse Effect definition excludes changes in applicable law or accounting standards, such as GAAP.

The proposed Material Adverse Effect definition provides that the loss of significant customers is excluded from the benefit of the MAE carve-outs and can still count toward a Material Adverse Effect.
The customer-concentration exception in the proposed Material Adverse Effect definition specifies a percentage-of-annual-revenue threshold for identifying a significant customer.
The proposed escrow deposit is a specific percentage greater than 7.5% and less than 20% of the $118,500,000 aggregate purchase price.
The memo states a dollar amount for the proposed escrow deposit that equals the stated percentage of the $118,500,000 aggregate purchase price.
The proposed escrow period is a specific duration of at least 12 months and no more than 24 months post-closing.
The proposed escrow arrangement provides for partial or staged release of escrow funds before the escrow period fully expires.
The rationale cites the ABA Private Target M&A Deal Points Study or an equivalent identifiable market benchmark study to justify at least one proposed compromise position.

The deliverable acknowledges or provides that Fundamental Representations (title to shares, authorization, capitalization, brokers) have a separate indemnification cap higher than the proposed general representation cap.
The proposed compromise states that the escrow is the Buyer’s sole and exclusive remedy for indemnification claims under general representations and warranties.
The sole-and-exclusive-remedy limitation expressly carves out Fundamental Representations from the escrow-only limitation.
The sole-and-exclusive-remedy limitation expressly carves out claims of fraud from the escrow-only limitation.
The deliverable includes proposed indemnification cap provision text written in a style and format suitable for insertion into a Stock Purchase Agreement.
The deliverable includes proposed survival period provision text written in a style and format suitable for insertion into a Stock Purchase Agreement.
The deliverable includes proposed Material Adverse Effect definition text written in a style and format suitable for insertion into a Stock Purchase Agreement.
The deliverable includes proposed escrow arrangement text written in a style and format suitable for insertion into a Stock Purchase Agreement or escrow agreement.

The deliverable acknowledges the Buyer’s demand for a quantitative MAE trigger based on any revenue or EBITDA decline exceeding 10% measured against the trailing twelve-month period, where TTM EBITDA is $19,750,000, and takes a position on that demand.
The deliverable incorporates the quantitative MAE trigger at a threshold different from the Buyer’s 10%.
The deliverable treats the quantitative MAE trigger as a non-exclusive indicator of a potential MAE rather than an automatic trigger.
The deliverable rejects the quantitative MAE trigger with rationale grounded in market practice or the ABA Deal Points Study data.
